results.verification: Vote counts and the 45.08% turnout on an electorate of 5,919 from KentOnline's report of the declaration. Every share reconciles to the independently published shares from electionmapsuk (Green 28.8, Reform 27.5, Con 17.1, Lab 14.6, Restore 10.7, Ind 1.3). Rejected papers are not published: the 4 here is 2,668 ballots less 2,664 valid votes, so replace it when Dover publishes the declaration.

Vote counts identical in the Hexham Courant's report of the declaration and on Wikipedia's 2026 Newcastle City Council election page, which also gives turnout as 32.9%, down 11.9 points on May. That reconciles with our own May 2026 record for the ward (44.77% on an electorate of 6,982). Rejected papers and the August electorate are not published, so both are left null rather than derived.

Full candidate counts and the 15.63% turnout from the Sheffield Star's report of the declaration, with the winner's 1,133 and the 297 margin corroborated by the syndicated LDRS copy. One search summary rendered the winning figure as 1,113, which does not reconcile with the published 297 margin over Labour's 836, so 1,133 is the figure. Rejected papers and the electorate are not published.

Primary. Wandsworth's own published voting summary: 3,283 valid votes, 7 rejected papers, electorate 8,319. Turnout here is computed as 3,290 of 8,319, which is 39.55%. The council's news release rounds it to 39.56%.
